videos.title: Meta's New Muse Wonder Is Huge!
videos.ai_tech_id: Meta Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full (Meta's generative AI app features, including Active Memory and Active Focus)
summary: Paul J Lipsky covers Meta's newly announced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, framing the release as a significant step up for Meta's AI creative tools rather than an incremental update.

He walks through Meta's own demo material for the two features, focusing on Active Memory (which lets the system retain context across a creative session) and Active Focus (which steers generation toward a specific subject or intent), and relays the benchmark figures Meta published to support its claims about the new models' capability.

The video closes by speculating on what Muse Wonder means for the broader Muse app, positioning it as a notable competitive move in the generative AI space that Meta is betting on to keep pace with other major AI labs.

videos.title: I Built the Ultimate AI Board of Advisors (free claude skill)
videos.ai_tech_id: Anthropic Claude Code sub-agents / Claude Skills (a free "Roast Room" multi-agent skill)
summary: Nate Herk introduces the "Roast Room," a system he built in Claude Code where seven AI sub-agents modeled on well-known business figures (including personas inspired by Jeff Bezos, Alex Hormozi, and Warren Buffett) debate a business decision and return a scored verdict, and he is giving the underlying skill away for free.

He walks through how the sub-agents are configured and what shapes each advisor's reasoning, demonstrates a live debate among the council over a sample decision, and shows how to install the free skill into a viewer's own Claude Code setup, including tips for phrasing questions so the advisors produce sharper, more useful pushback.

Framed for solo operators and AI agency builders, the video positions the Roast Room as a way to outsource the legwork of gathering diverse business perspectives while the human retains final judgment, and includes timestamped chapters covering setup, the advisor debate, and how to ask better questions.

videos.title: Robots at SF Tech Week
videos.ai_tech_id: Consumer/service humanoid robots from FF Robotics and Unitree (general robotics, no specific LLM or software platform named)
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shares a short, personal-style clip from SF Tech Week where she got an up-close look at humanoid and service robots from makers including FF Robotics and Unitree.

The video is light on technical detail and framed as an in-person reaction piece, contrasting the feel of seeing robots move through a crowd with watching a polished demo video online, and inviting viewers to react to which robot they'd want to meet first.

It reads as audience-engagement content for her AI/tech-focused following rather than a deep dive on any one product, using the robots as a hook to discuss how physical AI is starting to show up at industry events in San Francisco.

videos.title: Robots on the Runway at SF Tech Week
videos.ai_tech_id: Consumer/service humanoid robots in a crowd-judged exhibition format (general robotics, no specific LLM or software platform named)
summary: A follow-up clip from the same SF Tech Week coverage, this time showing robots competing in a runway-style exhibition judged live by the audience in attendance.

Sabrina Ramonov frames it as a lighthearted but genuine showcase of how far humanoid robotics has come, noting the novelty of a crowd picking a 'winner' among competing robot entries rather than reviewing a controlled lab demo.

Like the companion video posted a few hours earlier, it's built for engagement (asking viewers to vote on their favorite) rather than technical analysis, functioning as a window into the event's atmosphere rather than a product review.
